subject: technology
essential_question: How can understanding data science and computational models help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?
standards: Michigan Computer Science: Data and Analysis
project_brief: Analyze an approved dataset and publish a reproducible report with uncertainty and limits. This is the grade 8 culminating project for "Data Science and Computational Models" (ma-g8-technology-u04, unit 4), built around ethical data collection, cleaning and transformation, formulas and code, visualization, and correlation and model limitations. Analyze an approved dataset and publish a reproducible report with uncertainty and limits. As you build this, trace through your logic by hand for at least one representative input or scenario before you run or finalize it, so you can compare your prediction with the actual result.
requirements: Address every topic listed for this unit: ethical data collection, cleaning and transformation, formulas and code, visualization, correlation and model limitations, and data storytelling.
Meet the performance task as written: Analyze an approved dataset and publish a reproducible report with uncertainty and limits.
Show your work or process, not just a final result — a process note, sketch log, commit history, or draft trail.
Complete the checklist in this package before submitting.
primary_task: Analyze an approved dataset and publish a reproducible report with uncertainty and limits. As you build this, trace through your logic by hand for at least one representative input or scenario before you run or finalize it, so you can compare your prediction with the actual result.
test_or_check_criteria: Every claim or design choice in the submission can be traced to ethical data collection or another named topic from this unit — nothing is left unexplained.
The submission runs, displays, or demonstrates correctly on at least two different sample inputs or scenarios the student chooses.
No real password, API key, account credential, precise location, or other real personal/system data appears anywhere in the submission — fictional or sandbox examples only.
The student can explain, in their own words, why each step or decision was made, not just that it works.
The algorithm or program handles at least one edge case (empty input, zero, an unexpected choice) without crashing or giving a wrong answer silently.

presentation_and_privacy.sandbox_and_credentials_note: This project never touches a real account, a real password or API key, a live production system, or another person's real data. Use fictional names, sandbox environments, local files, or already-approved sample data throughout. Submit code, screenshots of your own sandbox, diagrams, or a written walkthrough — a live public deployment is never required.

copyright_and_authorship: The final submitted work must remain your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI assistant may help you plan, explain a concept, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but may not produce the graded work itself. Never request, store, or submit a real password, API key, access token, or other real credential; use only fictional accounts and sandboxed or offline systems.
remediation: If the project stalls, step back to the smallest version of the task: rebuild just the part covering ethical data collection in isolation, using a worked example from this unit as a model, then re-attach it to the full project once that smaller piece works and you can explain why.
extension: Once the core project is working, extend it to handle a new constraint or edge case related to cleaning and transformation, or compare two different approaches to the same problem and explain the real tradeoff between them in your own words.
